[protobuf] Wire generate and post-roll check CLI and README

`GenerateBootstrapFiles` and `CheckRoll` are in place, but
`roll_protobuf.py` still invokes `CheckTreeMatchesPatchedUpstream` from
`main()` and does not expose `generate` or `--baseline` on the command
line.

Users and automation need CLI flags for `generate -C <out_dir>` and
`check [-C <out_dir>] [--baseline <name>]`, `status` guidance that
advances from `generate` to `check` (while ignoring stale roll state on
unrelated branches), and updated `README.chromium` roll notes.

Wire `generate` and `check --baseline` in `main()`, update `StartRoll`,
`GetRollStatus`, `PrepareRoll`, `ContinueRoll`, `DropCurrentPatch`,
`ResumeRoll`, and `AbortRoll` to track active and orphaned roll branches
via `_IsRollBranchHead` and `_FindLocalRollBranch`, and document
`generate` and post-roll `check` in `README.chromium` with end-to-end
CLI tests.

[protobuf] Add CheckRoll and report formatting for check

Today `CheckTreeMatchesPatchedUpstream` checks only whether
`patches/*.patch` reproduces `//third_party/protobuf` from upstream and
produces a tree-diff report.

Post-roll verification needs a single result object and formatter that
combine blocking invariants (tree match, `README.chromium` patch
inventory sync, local checkout hygiene, and up-to-date bootstrap files)
with informational reports (`src/file_lists.cmake` changes and
`compile_size_probe.py` deltas) without turning size deltas into errors.

Add `RollCheckResult`, `CheckRoll`, and `FormatRollCheckReport`, sharing
`_DiffFileListsAgainstGitSpec` between `PlanRoll` and post-roll checks,
along with unit tests for clean, failing, and probe-error reports.

[protobuf] Add compile_size_probe.py comparison helpers for check

During a protobuf roll, header or codegen changes can trigger
`compile-size` or binary-size regressions whose root cause is hard to
spot from aggregate bot totals alone. `compile_size_probe.py` already
captures per-header `#include` chains and symbol byte deltas against a
saved baseline in `<out_dir>/.compile_size_probe/`.

Before wiring the full post-roll `roll_protobuf.py check`, `check` needs
optional, non-blocking helpers that discover a saved baseline (`before`,
`pre_roll`, or the newest `<name>.json` excluding `.artifacts.json`
sidecars), invoke `compile_size_probe.py --compare=<name> --json` as a
subprocess without importing it, and format a concise summary.

Add `_SelectCompileSizeBaseline`, `_RunCompileSizeProbeComparison`, and
`_FormatCompileSizeSummary` to `roll_protobuf.py`, along with hermetic
unit tests covering baseline auto-discovery, summary formatting, and
error handling.

[protobuf] Add patch-inventory, hygiene, and stale-bootstrap checks

Before uploading a protobuf roll, `roll_protobuf.py check` currently
verifies only that `patches/*.patch` reproduces the working tree from
upstream.

That check alone misses three pre-upload error classes: missing or
orphaned entries in `README.chromium` and `patches/*.md`, leftover
`.rej`/`.orig` files or conflict markers under `//third_party/protobuf`,
and checked-in bootstrap outputs left stale or un-staged after an
upstream import, a compiler edit, or an autosquash rebase.

Extract `FindPatchInventorySyncErrors` and `FindCompanionMarkdownErrors`
in `PRESUBMIT.py` (named `Find*` so `PRESUBMIT_VERSION = '2.0.0'` does
not auto-invoke them as presubmit entry points) so `PRESUBMIT.py` and
`roll_protobuf.py` share one implementation, and add
`_FindPatchInventoryErrors`, `_FindLocalHygieneErrors`, and
`_FindStaleBootstrapTriggers` in `roll_protobuf.py` with unit tests.

[protobuf] Add GenerateBootstrapFiles for roll_protobuf.py generate

After `roll_protobuf.py` imports a new upstream release and replays
`patches/*.patch`, Chromium's checked-in C++ and Python bootstrap files
(`descriptor.pb.{h,cc}`, `compiler/plugin.pb.{h,cc}`, `*_pb2.py`, and
`python_edition_defaults.py`) still reflect the pre-roll compiler.

Regenerating those files by hand requires running
`gen_extra_chromium_files.py`, staging any cleaned-up upstream paths,
force-adding gitignored `*_pb2.py` files, and keeping roll state in
sync. Follow-up `check` and `generate` CLI changes need a programmatic
step that performs this cleanly, restores the checkout on failure, and
records a digest of the generator inputs so stale bootstrap outputs can
be detected after later edits.

Add `IsBootstrapGeneratorInput`, `GenerateBootstrapFiles`, and
`FormatGenerateReport` to `roll_protobuf.py`, along with hermetic unit
tests covering gitignored outputs, empty re-runs, and failed runs.

[Linux] Prevent stale activation token reuse

Follow up on https://crrev.com/c/8605326.

A background launch can leave its activation token in global storage.
When a later launch opens a new window with another token, X11 replaces
that window's _NET_STARTUP_ID with the old token. Wayland can leave the
old token for a later activation instead.

Consume the stored token even when the command-line token takes
priority. Use it as the fallback when the command line has none.

Apply IWYU cleanup to the touched files.

[Vertical Tabs] Fix context menus appearing on tap, and multiple menus opening, on 2 finger presses

<After>
https://screencast.googleplex.com/cast/NTc1MzA1MTUzMTk2ODUxMnxhM2Q3YWYzYi02Mg

<Root Cause>
This only happens on touch screens on finger presses.
This bug has 2 issues:

Issue A (context menu appearing on tap):
Flow:
1) Finger 1 down on webpage (or resize handle) at say 0.0s
2) Finger 2 down (calls VT rail ACTION_DOWN) at say 2.0s
3) The touch events are split -- finger 1 event goes to the web page (or resize handle view) view, finger 2 event goes to the vt rail view
4) The catch: even though finger 2 touched the rail (eventTime), the event for finger 2 still carries finger 1's stop watch start time (downTime).
5) When Android's GestureDetector sees ACTION_DOWN on the rail, it sets a timer for
Long-Press Timer = downTime + 0.4s. Because downTime is 0.0s (from Finger 1), the timer is set for 0.4s, which is already in the past because eventTime for finger 2 is 2.0s.
6) GestureDetector thinks the finger has been held for 2 seconds, and fires onLongPress instantly on quick taps.

Issue B (multiple context menus opening):
Flow:
1) Suppose Context Menu #1 is already open on the rail, while Finger 1 is still held down on the webpage (or resize handle).
2) Normally (with one finger), touching anywhere outside Context Menu #1 causes Android's WindowManager to automatically dismiss Context Menu #1.
3) The catch: Because Finger 1 never left the screen, Android's WindowManager does not treat Finger 2 touching the rail as ACTION_OUTSIDE (which dismisses the context menu).
4) Furthermore, in VerticalTabListCoordinator (and TabStripContextMenuCoordinator / TabOverflowMenuCoordinator), when showEmptySpaceContextMenu() or
showTabItemContextMenu() is called to open Context Menu #2, it creates a brand-new PopupWindow without dismissing Context Menu #1 first.
5) Result: Context Menu #1 stays stuck on screen, and Context Menu #2 (and #3, #4...) stacks on top of it.

<Fix>
Issue A:
Fix Finger 2's downTime so that its long-press timer starts at Finger 2's own eventTime (2.0s + 0.4s = 2.4s). This way, a quick tap with finger 2 will not open a context menu, and a real long-press with finger 2 will open the context menu normally.

Issue B:
A new new touch-down on the rail dismisses any open rail context menus, which matches the mouse behavior.
Also added dismissActiveContextMenus() before showMenu() as safegaurds.

[Mac] Merge NativeWidgetNSWindow geometry requests into SetBounds

NativeWidgetNSWindow had four methods to change a window's geometry:
SetInitialBounds, SetBounds, SetSize and SetSizeAndCenter. Several of
them computed the resulting frame in the NSWindow's process, from
state that the host either did not track or could only see
asynchronously (the frame size for a content size, and where to
center the window). So for remote windows, the host could not know
the result of the request until the NSWindow reported it back.

Merge them into a single SetBounds(origin, size, ...), similar to
SetWindowPos(). The origin is optional, so that SetSize() can still
keep the window's top-left corner where it actually is (like
SWP_NOMOVE). All other frame computations move to the host:
- The frame size for a content size is computed from the window's
  style mask, which the host now tracks for remote windows.
- CenterWindow() computes the centered origin itself: over the
  visible part of the parent, clamped to the work area, as before.
- The frame size for empty initial bounds is computed from the
  window's style mask.

CenterWindow() now goes through SetBoundsInScreen(), so the host
applies the centered bounds right away, like for SetBounds().

Behavior change: windows without a parent used to be placed by
-[NSWindow center], i.e. centered horizontally and "somewhat above
center" vertically, in an undocumented way that the host cannot
compute. Like on other platforms, they are now centered in the work
area of their display.

This is in preparation for tagging geometry requests with ids, so
that stale geometry reports can be ignored.

[gtk] Lazily load GTK theme colors on demand in GtkUi

GtkUi::Initialize() and GtkUi::OnThemeChanged() previously called
LoadGtkValues() eagerly, building a SystemTheme::kGtk ColorProvider and
querying GTK CSS even when Chrome uses the default theme
(SystemTheme::kDefault).

Since ColorProviderManager and GetBgColor()/GetFgColor() (via
GetStyleColorCache()) already cache these colors and invalidate them on
theme or accent changes, drop LoadGtkValues() and the duplicate cached
color members on GtkUi, and query them on demand in the color getters
(matching QtUi).

On Linux Crossbench browser-startup (--separate --repeat=32,
newtab_startup):
- Startup.BrowserWindow.FirstPaint: 534.0 ms -> 512.0 ms (-28.0 ms /
  -5.2% paired median, p=0.024).
- InitialWebUI.Startup.ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint: 571.5 ms ->
  555.5 ms (-27.5 ms / -4.8% paired median, p=0.026).
- Startup.FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3: 678.0 ms -> 662.5 ms
  (-13.0 ms / -1.9% paired median).

[DTC] Add LINT checks for EnterpriseSignals variants

GetHistogramVariant() in metrics_utils.cc is the single source of the
{Signal} token used by the Enterprise.DeviceSignals.Collection.*
histograms, but nothing tied it to the "EnterpriseSignals" variants
block in histograms.xml, which is how the Agent and Certificates
variants ended up undeclared.

Wrap both sides in matching LINT.IfChange/LINT.ThenChange blocks so that
adding a SignalName case to GetHistogramVariant() without updating the
XML variants (or vice versa) is flagged by presubmit.

content: Hide window.SharedWorker when shared workers are disallowed

When a WebContents is created with
PrivilegedParams::disallow_shared_workers,
SharedWorkerServiceImpl::ConnectToWorker rejects shared worker
connections in the browser process. However, window.SharedWorker
remained exposed in Blink, breaking pages that use standard feature
detection ('SharedWorker' in window) to fall back when shared workers
are unavailable.

Give the SharedWorker runtime-enabled feature
browser_process_read_write_access and disable it via
RuntimeFeatureStateContext in NavigationRequest::ReadyToCommitNavigation
when the hosting WebContents disallows shared workers, while retaining
the browser-process check in SharedWorkerServiceImpl::ConnectToWorker as
defense in depth.

[metrics] Fix dirmd pipe deadlock in expand_owners.py

ExtractComponentViaDirmd() called Popen.wait() before reading dirmd's
stdout. When dirmd output exceeds the OS pipe buffer (64 KiB on Linux),
dirmd blocks on write and Python blocks on wait(), hanging
//tools/metrics:histograms_xml and metrics_python_tests until the build
times out. This happened after //base/android opted into large
agentic_review mixins (~81 KB of sparse dirmd output), see
crrev.com/c/8638149 and its revert crrev.com/c/8661579.

Use subprocess.run(capture_output=True) so the output is drained while
dirmd runs, and add a regression test with a fake dirmd that emits
~200 KB of output.

Remove allow_circular_includes_from from //third_party/grpc:grpc++_h

upb/reflection/descriptor_bootstrap.h in :upb_reflection_internal_lib
includes google/protobuf/descriptor.upb.h, which was listed in
:grpc++_h. :grpc++_h depends on :upb_reflection_internal_lib, so the
include needed allow_circular_includes_from.

Move descriptor.upb.h, descriptor.upb_minitable.h and
descriptor.upb_minitable.c into a new :upb_descriptor_upb_proto_lib,
and upb/generated_code_support.h, which they include, into a new
:upb_generated_code_support_lib. :upb_reflection_internal_lib depends
on the former, and :grpc++_h depends publicly on both so that
:grpc++_cc and :grpc++_repeated* can keep including these headers.

Remove the entry from circular_includes_untriaged.gni.

Part of LSC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LuFqCJwtzZHuLfoj9yuupZnlCqwnbDXBgmF70tCwxDE/edit?tab=t.0

Revert "Reland "[contextual_tasks] Allow deselecting submitted and restored tabs""

This reverts commit e17ac940a5c70d17afc4ef4bd221c573f496a733.

Reason for revert: Causes
ContextualTasksExtensionHandlerBrowserTest.GetRecentTabs_IncludesAttachedInternalTabAndAllowsDeselection
to time out on linux-chromeos-chrome. DeleteTabContext early returns
when a tab is submitted but enable_tab_deselection is not enabled,
preventing OnTabContextUpdated notification.

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666830757953502625

Original change's description:
> Reland "[contextual_tasks] Allow deselecting submitted and restored tabs"
>
> This is a reland of commit df6e9ee0108b12bb15e7ef8798718a77ce5931fd
>
> Original change's description:
> > [contextual_tasks] Allow deselecting submitted and restored tabs
> >
> > The tab picker could only deselect tabs attached in the current turn.
> > DeleteTabContext() only searched unsubmitted tabs, so clicking a tab
> > submitted in an earlier turn, or a tab restored from the AIM thread, did
> > nothing and its checkmark came back on the next update.
> >
> > - Submitted tabs are now deleted through DeleteFile(), which keeps
> >   their request ID so the next submission reports them in
> >   removed_contexts. Like DeleteFile(), this requires tab deselection
> >   (ContextManagementInComposebox:enable_tab_deselection). Without it,
> >   submitted tabs stay attached rather than disappearing only from the
> >   UI while the server keeps using them.
> > - Restored tabs have no context token, so they are hidden locally and
> >   recorded as deselected. Later thread updates from AIM then keep them
> >   hidden while the tab stays on the same page.
> > - After a turn, AIM's thread update also restores the submitted tabs,
> >   so a tab can be both. Deselecting it removes both copies, since the
> >   restored copy would otherwise keep it selected.
> >
> > Bug: b:573759643
> > Change-Id: Idc9d69c4b13dd2c72eb673eac977d36a94c6fe7d
> > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8576728

> > Reviewed-by: Jason Hu <hujasonx@google.com>

[fuchsia] Shard blink_unittests and content_unittests on x64-asan

On fuchsia-fyi-x64-asan, blink_unittests and content_unittests run on a
single shard and take 45-60+ minutes, repeatedly hitting Swarming's
60-minute hard timeout (for example:
https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666896140332281313 and
https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666957343892690049).

Shard both test suites across 4 shards so each shard completes in ~15
minutes, matching components_unittests on the same builder.

[chromecast] Validate Host/Origin and prevent traversal in ui_devtools

UiDevToolsServer listens on a local TCP port. This CL hardens
UiDevToolsServer and GetSourceCode against unauthorized cross-origin
requests and path traversal:

1. Adds strict Host and Origin header verification inside
UiDevToolsServer::OnWebSocketRequest using net::IsLocalhost and
HostIsIPAddress to reject WebSocket requests from external origins.

2. Verifies that the resolved path in GetSourceCode is strictly
contained within base::DIR_SRC_TEST_DATA_ROOT to prevent arbitrary file
reads via directory traversal.

Replace ShapeResultBloberizer nested subclasses with factory methods

ShapeResultBloberizer previously defined nested structs (FillGlyphsNG,
FillTextEmphasisGlyphsNG, FillGlyphs, and an undefined forward
declaration FillTextEmphasisGlyphs) that publicly inherited from
ShapeResultBloberizer to provide named construction before C++17
guaranteed copy elision.

Replace those nested subclasses with inline static factory methods
FillGlyphs() and FillTextEmphasisGlyphs() returning
ShapeResultBloberizer by value, and make all ShapeResultBloberizer
constructors private.

No behavior changes.

[BrowserActuator] Replace GetOrCreateSession with CreateSession

Follow up on https://chromium-review.git.corp.google.com/c/chromium/src/+/8616904,
replaces `GetOrCreateSession` with `CreateSession` on
`TransportSessionRegistry` and `TransportService`, changes
`TransportChannelImpl::OnStreamMessage` to look up existing
sessions via `GetSessionImpl`, and removes `closed_session_ids_`
from `TransportSessionRegistryImpl`.

In `BrowserActuatorMessageHandler::OnMessage`, `CreateSession` is
now only called when a `ControlCommand::StartSession` payload is
received, while all other payloads resolve an existing active
session via `GetSession`. Downstream `WatchSessions` stream
messages and non-`StartSession` FCM wake-ups no longer create or
resurrect closed sessions, and duplicate `StartSession` wake-up
retries can be differentiated from initial session creation.

Changes:
- Replace `GetOrCreateSession` with `CreateSession` on
  `TransportSessionRegistry`, `TransportSessionRegistryImpl`,
  `TransportService`, `TransportServiceImpl`, and
  `MockTransportService`.
- Return `nullptr` in `TransportSessionRegistryImpl::CreateSession`
  when `session_id` is already active.
- Switch `TransportChannelImpl::OnStreamMessage` from
  `GetOrCreateSession` to `GetSessionImpl` and remove
  `closed_session_ids_` from `TransportSessionRegistryImpl`.
- Update `BrowserActuatorMessageHandler::OnMessage` to call
  `CreateSession` only on `ControlCommand::StartSession` payloads
  and `GetSession` on all other payloads.
- Update unit tests and add
  `IgnoresDownstreamMessageForUnknownSession` to
  `TransportChannelImplTest`.

[gtk] Prefetch window-control icons for the native browser frame

With the GTK system theme, the first browser window's `Widget::Init()`
computes its minimum size, which calls
`NavButtonProviderGtk::RedrawImages()`. On GTK3 this synchronously
decodes each `window-*-symbolic.svg` icon only to learn its size, and
the first paint decodes the icons again. gdk-pixbuf >= 2.43 decodes
through glycin, which uses a sandboxed loader process and a new thread
pool per conversion, so these decodes block the UI thread for ~300 ms
during startup.

Behind the `GtkPrefetchNavButtonIcons` feature (disabled by default):
- Size probes skip decoding `-symbolic.svg` icons whose directory `Size`
  and `Scale` match the lookup request, since GTK rasterizes them at
  `kNavButtonIconSize * scale`.
- When the first browser-frame `NavButtonProviderGtk` is created, start
  asynchronous loads of the minimize/maximize/close icons with the
  context that painting uses (normal, active, restored, 1x). Finishing
  a load fills the `GtkIconInfo` symbolic icon cache, so the first
  paint is a cache hit. Paints with other parameters fall back to the
  existing synchronous load.

Only GTK3 is affected. GTK4 (GNOME on Wayland) already loads these
icons in ~2 ms. The provider is only created for the native GTK frame,
so users of other themes don't pay for the prefetch.

Crossbench, browser_startup probes, newtab_startup story, --separate,
browser_startup initial_webui flags, fresh profile, Xvfb + openbox,
X11, 30 runs per arm. Median difference vs. feature off, with 95%
bootstrap CI and Mann-Whitney U p-value:

GTK theme:
  ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint  1084 -> 874 ms
                                     -210 ms [-246, -198], p = 3e-11
  BrowserWindow.FirstPaint           -185 ms [-218, -178], p = 3e-11
  FirstWebContents.NonEmptyPaint3    -193 ms [-232, -154], p = 6e-11
Classic theme (no native frame):
  ReloadButton.FirstContentfulPaint    +4 ms [-12, +20], p = 0.55
  BrowserWindow.FirstPaint             +4 ms [-10, +24], p = 0.12

[context-input] Add UMA metrics for UpdateThreadContextLibrary

Adds browser-side telemetry for handling UpdateThreadContextLibrary
messages received from AI Mode in Contextual Tasks:
- ContextualTasks.ThreadContextLibrary.UpdateOutcome: records the
  handling result across early-return and success paths (feature
  disabled, no session handle, empty converted context, or success
  with/without task ID).
- ContextualTasks.ThreadContextLibrary.CommittedContextCount: number of
  URL resources converted from the update message.
- ContextualTasks.ThreadContextLibrary.CommittedTabContextCount: number
  of tab-derived URL resources in the update message.
- ContextualTasks.ThreadContextLibrary.RestoredTabCount: number of
  tab-derived URL resources resolved to open tabs in the browser
  window.
- ContextualTasks.ThreadContextLibrary.TimeFromHandshakeToFirstUpdate:
  latency from postMessage handshake completion (or OnPageChanged) to
  the first UpdateThreadContextLibrary message for that page state.

[Wayland] Describe the primary plane's real HDR peak to the compositor

Previously, when Chromium output HDR to a Wayland compositor using
wp_color_management_v1, the primary plane had no HDR metadata.
WaylandWpColorManager then sent:
  * set_luminances(0, 1000, ref): the 1000 is a hardcoded fallback that
    is ignored for PQ.
  * set_max_cll(ref) / set_max_fall(ref): a workaround from
    crrev.com/c/7113272.

How compositors use these values:
  * KWin ignores the max of set_luminances for PQ and takes the content
    peak from max_cll, falling back to the mastering max luminance, and
    then to 10000 nits. It tone maps the surface if that peak exceeds
    the display peak. Without max_cll, a PQ surface was treated as
    10000 nits and tone mapped heavily, which made SDR content dark on
    KWin 6.5. That is the issue the workaround hid.
  * With max_cll = ref, KWin skips tone mapping and clips at the
    content peak. Since KWin 6.8 (KWin commit cc7635e4fe, "always clip
    to source range") the shader path clips at the source peak, so all
    HDR highlights in composited video were clipped to SDR white.
  * mutter ignores max_cll/max_fall and doesn't advertise mastering
    metadata, but it raises a protocol error if the reference luminance
    exceeds the set_luminances max.

SkiaRenderer already tone maps all HDR content to the display's HDR
headroom, so the actual peak of the primary plane is known. This CL:
  * Computes primary plane HDR metadata in viz on Ozone. When the root
    render pass has HDR content, max_cll and the mastering max are set
    to SDR white × the display's HDR headroom; otherwise they are set
    to SDR white. max_fall is SDR white. KWin then neither tone maps
    (so SDR doesn't get dark) nor clips HDR highlights. This replaces
    the max_cll = ref workaround with correct values.
  * Cleans up the creator params sent by WaylandWpColorManager:
    - The set_luminances max is the content peak (>= the reference
      luminance), for PQ too. The protocol says it is ignored for PQ,
      but Hyprland tone maps when it exceeds the display peak, so
      sending 10000 would dim the whole surface there. mutter requires
      it to be >= the reference luminance.
    - max_cll is never below the reference luminance, and max_fall
      never exceeds max_cll.
    - When mastering luminance is sent, its max is never below the
      reference luminance, and max_cll/max_fall are clamped to it.
      Weston raises a protocol error if they exceed it.
    - When CLLI is missing, max_cll falls back to the content's max
      luminance (1000 nits by default), which matches what viz assumes
      when tone mapping. This only affects overlays now.
    - Mastering primaries are only sent if valid, and luminances are
      capped at 10000.
  * Adds a wp_color_manager_v1 implementation to the Wayland test
    server, plus ozone_unittests covering the primary plane with HDR
    and SDR content, an overlay with MDCV/CLLI, an overlay without
    metadata, CLL below the reference luminance (PQ and HLG),
    compositors without mastering support, CLL above the mastering
    peak, and a mastering peak below the reference luminance. The test
    server rejects a reference luminance above the max luminance (like
    mutter) and CLL/FALL above the mastering peak (like Weston). Adds
    viz_unittests for the primary plane metadata.

[Capture] Clean up picker on window or tab close

When the window that opened the Android screen-share picker is closed
while the picker is showing, the native picker bridge is destroyed but
the picker's tab observers keep running. The next tab update in another
window calls into the destroyed bridge and crashes. A picker result
that arrives after its request is gone hits the same destroyed bridge.

Fix this by:
- Cancelling the pending picker request when its window is destroyed,
  but not when it's recreated for a config change, so the picker's tab
  observers are removed with the window.
- Cancelling, instead of starting a capture, when a result arrives
  after the request or its tab is gone, or when the picked tab can no
  longer be shared.
- Making the Java bridge ignore calls once its native side is gone.

Clank's picker delegate keeps the tab picked in the system picker
until a tab capture starts. Cancelling a late result skips that, so
the pick would be left behind and shared by the next window or screen
pick. A separate Clank change drops an unused pick when the picker
finishes, and must land before this CL.

Cancelling during multi-window teardown also exposed a
TabModelSelectorTabObserver bug: when it's destroyed in the same UI
turn it was created, it reports existing tabs as unregistered before
reporting them as registered. Skip onTabUnregistered() for tabs whose
onTabRegistered() hasn't run yet.

windows, close that window via caption X and navigate the other
window. Expect no crash.

chrome: Start network cookie and storage flush when shutdown begins

BrowserProcessIOThread::ProcessHostCleanUp() blocks the main thread
during late shutdown waiting for the network service utility process
to flush cookies and cache to disk, and is blamed in 3.6% of ChromeOS
shutdown hang reports. Trigger asynchronous FlushCookieStore() and
StoragePartition::Flush() calls across all loaded profiles in
browser_shutdown::OnShutdownStarting() so persistence overlaps with
browser window and profile teardown on all desktop platforms.

Reland "cros: Fast-shutdown renderers and skip window hide animation on exit"

Unchanged reland of 6ba4e77d8b5f (crrev.com/c/8615715), reverted in
crrev.com/c/8655438 after ChromeOS MSan browser tests hit a
~ProcessManager() UAF when FastShutdownIfPossible() with
ignore_workers=true killed a RenderProcessHost while an extension
service worker was initializing. Parent CL crrev.com/c/8653600 fixes
that observer lifetime bug in extensions/.

On ChromeOS, session_manager enforces a 3 s SIGTERM timeout across
ShouldIgnoreUnloadHandlers() and ShutdownType::kBrowserExit. Passing
skip_unload_handlers, ignore_workers, ignore_keep_alive, and
ignore_pending_reuse to FastShutdownIfPossible() terminates renderers
with service workers or fetch(keepalive) requests immediately without
affecting browser-side NavigationController session restore state, and
BrowserView::Close() skips visibility-change animations once shutdown
starts so wm::WindowAnimations does not clone the window layer tree.

extensions: Clean up service worker observations on RPH destruction

When RenderProcessHostImpl::FastShutdownIfPossible() runs with
ignore_workers=true while an extension service worker is starting,
FastShutdown() marks the host dead and fires RenderProcessExited()
while worker_ref_count_ keeps it alive. A queued ServiceWorkerHost
bind or DidInitializeServiceWorkerContext() IPC can then add the dead
host to ProcessManager::process_observations_, after which Cleanup()
only fires RenderProcessHostDestroyed() and ~ProcessManager() UAFs.
Ignore late ServiceWorkerHost binds and initialization IPCs on dead
hosts, and untrack hosts in RenderProcessHostDestroyed().

78d69396590f99ceafa191fc8fdc5f79250f0f73 [ diff ] 
[Android] Check IME visibility directly in isAndroidSoftKeyboardShowing

In split-screen or multi-window mode (e.g., when Chrome is in the top
split-screen pane), the window is resized above the soft keyboard so the
IME bottom inset is 0 even while the soft keyboard is visible.
Previously, KeyboardUtils.isAndroidSoftKeyboardShowing checked
calculateKeyboardHeightFromWindowInsets(rootView) > 0, and
ActivityKeyboardVisibilityDelegate checked inset > 0 to determine
whether the keyboard was showing.

This CL:
1. Updates KeyboardUtils.isAndroidSoftKeyboardShowing to check
        WindowInsetsCompat.isVisible(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.ime())
        directly when SplitScreenImeInsetVisibility is enabled, while
        keeping calculateKeyboardHeightFromWindowInsets returning 0
        when the IME bottom inset is 0.
2. Updates
        ActivityKeyboardVisibilityDelegate.onKeyboardInsetChanged to
        check isKeyboardShowing(content) instead of inset > 0 when
        SplitScreenImeInsetVisibility is enabled.

[PM] Handle SurfaceEmbed detach after the embedder frame is removed

The embedder frame node of a SurfaceEmbed child page can leave the graph
while the child is still attached, e.g. when the embedder's renderer
process dies. FrameNodeImpl::OnBeforeLeavingGraph() then clears the
page's embedder frame node & the child links, but content still sends
SurfaceEmbedChildWebContentsDetached() when the child is detached later.
That hit the CHECK that the page still has an embedder frame node.

Only clear the embedder frame node if it is still set.

[chromecast] Restrict Cast browser service to in-process Mojo clients

ExternalMojoBroker previously treated clients connecting over its Unix
domain socket identically to in-process connectors created via
CreateConnector() or BindConnector(). An external process able to
connect to the broker socket could bind or register internal browser
services such as chromecast::mojom::kCastBrowserServiceName.

Track whether each ExternalConnector and ServiceManagerConnectorFacade
receiver is in-process, configure BrokerService in CastBrowserMainParts
with kCastBrowserServiceName as an in-process-only service, and reject
external attempts to register or bind in-process-only services.

In PrepareSystemWebAppWindowForOnTask, a CHECK_NE assertion was recently
converted from DCHECK_NE as part of a bulk CHECK conversion. This
assertion can be triggered in production, causing crashes. Reverting the
macro back to DCHECK_NE prevents production crashes without altering
underlying behavior.

crash/973bdab408400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more details.

Revert the CHECK_EQ macro in ArcSessionManager's
MaybeStartTermsOfServiceNegotiation back to DCHECK_EQ. The state check
was converted to a fatal CHECK as part of a bulk conversion effort,
causing fatal crashes when state is not STOPPED. Using DCHECK_EQ avoids
crashing in production until the state precondition is properly
investigated.

crash/c85b459308400000. Please see go/crash-autofix for more details.

[chromecast] Remove unused ActivityUrlFilter and renderer throttles

ActivityUrlFilter, CastActivityUrlFilterManager,
ActivityUrlFilterConfiguration, ActivityFilteringURLLoaderThrottle, and
ActivityFilteringWebSocketHandshakeThrottle were created for legacy Cast
OS Activities and are never populated in production
(CastWebViewParams::url_filters is never set).

Remove this dead code to clean up unused per-frame Mojo bindings and
renderer URL/WebSocket throttles, and use url::Origin comparison for
additional feature permission origins in CastPermissionManager.

[ash] cloud_upload: stop re-exporting platform_util.h

cloud_upload_util.h and one_drive_upload_handler.h include
chrome/browser/platform_util.h without naming anything from it. Two
files were reaching platform_util through them --
file_manager_test_util.cc and cloud_upload_dialog_browsertest.cc, both
of which call platform_util::OpenItem and friends -- so they include it
directly now and the two headers drop it.

No DEPS or build changes: both directories already allow
+chrome/browser/platform_util.h for the files that use it.

db0d27b32b9096ac673be24f4e41287ed9f66e1d [ diff ] 
[Blink] Fix allowed_touch_action DCHECK in InputHandlerProxy::HandleTouchMove

InputHandlerProxy::HitTestTouchEvent computes an allowed touch action
if and only if `touch_event.touch_start_or_first_touch_move` is true,
previously enforcing `DCHECK(!allowed_touch_action)` on non-first
TouchMove events via its out-parameter.

However, `InputHandlerProxy::HandleTouchMove` enters its hit-testing
block whenever `!touch_result_.has_value() ||
touch_event.touch_start_or_first_touch_move` holds (for example, when
early events in a touch sequence are suppressed before First Contentful
Paint and a subsequent TouchMove arrives with
`touch_start_or_first_touch_move == false` and an empty
`touch_result_`). Previously, `HandleTouchMove` unconditionally passed
`&allowed_touch_action` to `HitTestTouchEvent` and reported the
uncomputed default `TouchAction::kAuto` via `SetAllowedTouchAction`.

Update `HitTestTouchEvent` to return a `HitTestTouchEventResult` struct
containing both the `EventDisposition` and an
`std::optional<cc::TouchAction>` (populated only when
`touch_event.touch_start_or_first_touch_move` is true), and invoke
`client_->SetAllowedTouchAction` in `HandleTouchMove` only when
`touch_event.touch_start_or_first_touch_move` is true.

[Base] Re-enable MemoryDumpManagerTest.RegistrationConsistency on iOS

RegistrationConsistency was disabled on iOS in 2017 by
crrev.com/2787823004 (9770fad0b3ebe) because it "seemed flaky" while
MemoryDumpManager was about to be restructured to not know about
tracing; the cause was intentionally never investigated
(crbug.com/706961, referenced in the comment as crbug.com/706874).
That restructuring landed long ago: the test now only checks that a
dump provider registered on the current SingleThreadTaskRunner is
invoked exactly as many times as its current registration state
implies, through RequestProcessDumpAndWait(), which blocks until the
dump callback has run and no longer depends on tracing being enabled.

No new test is added: this CL only restores existing coverage on iOS.
The test was run 9 times on iPhone 17 Pro Max (iOS 26.4) and iPad Pro
11-inch M5 (iOS 26.0) simulators and passed every time.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

Mark TextInputState updated on active_view_ transitions

`TextInputManager::UpdateTextInputState` caches `TextInputState`
even when an unfocused view cannot become `active_view_`. If that
view later regains focus and reports the same state,
`ShouldUpdateTextInputState` returns `false` despite `active_view_`
changing, which causes `RenderWidgetHostViewAura` to skip
`InputMethod::OnTextInputTypeChanged`.

Set `changed = true` whenever `active_view_` changes so observers
are notified of the active view transition.

Camera capture: Pass enumeration modes through the video capture service

This change adds a video enumeration mode to
`VideoSourceProvider::GetSourceInfos()` and carries it through the video
capture service to `VideoCaptureSystem`.

`VideoCaptureSystemImpl` tracks whether its cached device information
includes capabilities. DeviceFactoryImpl uses this to decide if it
should trigger a `kDevicesWithCapabilities` enumeration before the
device is created.

This CL updates the `VideoSourceProvider` mojom interface.
`VideoCaptureProvider` will be updated in a follow-up CL. For now,
`ServiceVideoCaptureProvider` passes `kDevicesWithCapabilities` to
preserve existing browser-initiated enumeration behavior.

[3p freshness] sentencepiece: Add Crowbar workflow

Replace roll.sh with a Crowbar workflow that does the same import, so
the dependency can be updated with Crowbar.

- crowbar.txtpb: https://github.com/google/sentencepiece at the
  README.chromium Revision, b9e2e4f6ebc73900e061044b54f68a95090e23ff.
- copy.bara.sky: imports the files roll.sh copied, porting its rsync
  excludes. rsync matches a single-component pattern (data/, python/,
  .github/, BUILD, ...) at any depth, so those get both a top-level
  and a "**/" glob. Then applies the existing patches, in roll.sh's
  order.
- patches/: paths rewritten from a/third_party/sentencepiece/src/ to
  a/src/ because Crowbar applies patches with src/ as the prefix. The
  changes themselves are unchanged.
- README.chromium: Crowbar instructions replace roll.sh in "Rolling",
  and "Making new patches" uses --relative so new patches get the
  same prefix.
- Delete roll.sh.

src/ does not change. The workflow reproduces it exactly:

  $ crowbar build ./third_party/sentencepiece
  Package third_party/sentencepiece is already up-to-date.

Dropping an exclude for contrib/docker, contrib/nlcodec, data, python,
third_party/protobuf-lite or .github, or any patch, makes the same
command change src/. The other excludes change nothing today and are
kept as in roll.sh.

Mojo Java: Move repeated interface binding code into the runtime

Shrinks Chrome's dex by 35kb.

Generated Java mojom interface bindings repeated a lot of boilerplate
for every interface and every method. This moves it into shared runtime
code:
 * *ProxyToResponder classes extend a new ProxyToResponder base class,
   which holds their fields and serializes / sends responses.
 * *ForwardToCallback classes extend a new ForwardToCallback base class,
   which validates response headers and wraps deserialization errors.
 * Proxy methods use new AbstractProxy.sendMessage() and
   sendMessageWithResponder() helpers.
 * Stubs no longer override accept() / acceptWithResponder(). Instead,
   Stub validates flags, handles interface control messages, and
   dispatches to generated handleMessage() / handleMessageWithResponder()
   methods.
 * Manager's getName() / getVersion() are passed to its constructor
   rather than being overridden.

Behavior is unchanged.

f4d6f32e1bbd63b4c72c706a110d30d0d9299358 [ diff ] 
SuperSize: Cache DeltaSymbol.diff_status

diff_status is queried ~8 times per DeltaSymbol when diffing with
sort=True and describing the result (clustering, filtering, counting,
and formatting), and each query computes size and PSS deltas. Compute
it once per DeltaSymbol.

This assumes before_symbol / after_symbol are not modified after
diffing, which holds for diff.Diff() callers.

Expected speed-up: diff.Diff(sort=True) + describe.GenerateLines() on
two ~2.1M-symbol .size files (as done by trybot_commit_size_checker.py):
58.87s -> 54.02s (identical output).

[context-input] Sync the side panel's task with its AI Mode thread

In the side panel rearchitecture, the panel hosts the AI Mode page
directly, so nothing mapped its thread (`mtid`) to its task, unlike the
legacy WebUI (`ContextualTasksUI::FrameNavObserver`) and full-tab AI
Mode (`ContextualTasksTabNavigationObserver`). The panel's task never
got its thread, and a new chat kept the previous thread's task, so its
submits used the previous thread's task and selected tabs.

Add `ContextualTasksPanelThreadObserver` to the panel's AI Mode
WebContents:
- Like `ContextualTasksTabNavigationObserver`, the panel's task follows
  its thread: the thread is added to the panel's task, and the panel
  moves to the task of another thread (e.g. picked from history),
  created if needed.
- When the page reports zero state with `OnPageChanged` after a turn
  (e.g. "New chat"), the panel moves to a new task, before the input
  state and implicit tab are updated for the new conversation. This also
  covers signed-out AI Mode, whose turns have `mstk` but no `mtid`.
Task changes go through `ContextualTasksUiService::OnTaskChanged()`,
which also moves the tabs associated with the panel's task. Share the
`mtid` parsing and thread update with
`ContextualTasksTabNavigationObserver`.

The observer is attached to each side panel AI Mode WebContents, whether
created, rebuilt or moved from a tab, and is removed when one is moved
to a tab, which `ContextualTasksTabNavigationObserver` then handles.

Post-rearchitecture,
`ContextualTasksSidePanelCoordinator::OnTaskChanged()` now updates the
reporting panel WebContents if it is cached, rather than always the
active one.

Remove deprecated kMouseHover from ai_page_content.mojom

Removes the deprecated kMouseHover clickability reason from
ai_page_content.mojom and page_content_proto_util.

In Chromium, Mojom is strictly unversioned IPC between the Blink
renderer and browser processes within the same Chrome release.
Because modern Blink and iOS extractions have switched to emitting
kMouseEnter and kMouseOver, kMouseHover has no producers and no
consumers in Mojo. (The legacy CLICKABILITY_REASON_MOUSE_HOVER enum
value is retained in common_quality_data.proto to interpret historical
serialized datasets and goldens).

This change:
1. Removes kMouseHover from AIPageContentClickabilityReason in
   ai_page_content.mojom.
2. Removes the kMouseHover case from ToProtoClickabilityReason in
   page_content_proto_util.cc.
3. Updates unit tests in page_content_proto_util_unittest and
   ai_page_content_agent_unittest.

R=joenotcharles@google.com, linnan@chromium.org

[SafeBrowsing] Fix and re-enable TestCleanUpExpiredVerdict on iOS

Fix time-truncation bugs in
VerdictCacheManagerTest.TestCleanUpExpiredVerdict and re-enable it on
iOS devices.

VerdictCacheManagerTest uses TaskEnvironment::TimeSource::MOCK_TIME,
which initializes base::Time::Now() from system uptime snapped to 1 ms.
This caused two failures in TestCleanUpExpiredVerdict (disabled on iOS
devices in crrev.com/c/3252144 and crrev.com/c/4086310):

1. VerdictCacheManagerTest::CreatePageLoadToken() took a 32-bit int
   token_time_msec instead of int64_t. When a device's uptime exceeded
   INT32_MAX ms (~24.85 days, common on persistent iOS lab devices),
   now.InMillisecondsSinceUnixEpoch() overflowed 32-bit int, causing
   CleanUpExpiredPageLoadTokens() to evict the valid token2.
2. CreateDictionaryFromVerdict() truncates receive_time to whole seconds
   and IsCacheExpired() checks Now() > cache_creation_time + duration.
   Calling CleanUpExpiredVerdicts() without advancing the clock meant
   entries with cache_duration_sec = 0 only expired if now had a
   non-zero millisecond component, failing when now landed on an exact
   second (1 in 1,000 runs).

Change CreatePageLoadToken() to accept int64_t, advance the mock clock
by 1 second before CleanUpExpiredVerdicts(), and re-enable the test.

Part of http://go/arthurmilchior-fix-all-test-skill-chrome for AI week.

media: Stream biplanar video conversion through libyuv

Write RGB-to-NV16/NV24 and RGB-to-P010/P210/P410 directly into the
output planes. Convert 8-bit planar input to Px10 with row workspace
instead of full-frame 16-bit chroma planes.

Use direct Px10-to-I420 conversion and the matching planar 10-bit
libyuv entry points. Scale 8-bit NV output after reducing the input
bit depth, avoiding full-frame planar 10-bit intermediates. This
changes rounding compared with scaling before bit-depth reduction.
Use Px10 scalers to process Y and UV in separate allocation phases.

In warmed 3840x2160 libyuv pipeline microbenchmarks on an M1 Pro,
RGB-to-P010/P210/P410 throughput improves by 1.19x/1.12x/1.18x.
Px10-to-NVxx downscaling improves by 1.4x-1.9x. These are conversion
pipeline measurements, not end-to-end encoder measurements. Existing
Arm and x86 SIMD dispatch is preserved.

At 3840x2160, RGB-to-P410 temporary frame storage drops from 55.37
MiB to 18.75 KiB of row workspace. I444-to-P410 chroma workspace drops
from 31.64 MiB to 15 KiB. For P010 scaling from 4K to 1080p, peak
frame workspace falls from 29.66 MiB to 15.82 MiB, excluding scaler
row buffers and frame padding. Same-format Px10 scaling was slower
on this CPU and is retained for its lower memory usage.

Share 16-bit plane accessors to keep strides in sample units and
remove repeated casts. Centralize the matching planar format mappings.
Keep the existing planar 10/12-bit-to-Px10 implementation, where the
higher-level APIs offer no advantage.

Add focused sample-exact coverage for RGB byte orders, odd cropped
frames, 8-to-10-bit expansion, ten-bit MSB scaling, and filtered I420
chroma reduction. Check scratch-frame use and extend output coverage
to P410 without changing existing tests.

Support Android model solution config replacement

Allow component-provided AndroidManifest snapshots to override built-in
configs, retaining built-in fallbacks for omitted features. Keep the
snapshot in ModelBrokerAndroid, initializing built-ins lazily when the
solution factory is first initialized.

Make AndroidManifest copyable and movable, with copies preserving the
snapshot ID. Manifest-backed solutions compare their snapshot IDs with
the broker's active manifest. A different snapshot invalidates those
solutions so the shared SolutionProvider can publish replacements.
Adaptation-backed sessions, such as Scam Detection, remain unaffected.

Handle load results through OnManifestLoaded, preserving the current
snapshot on failure. New sessions use the replacement config. Sessions
tied to an invalidated solution cannot start further executions, but
in-flight executions can complete safely.

Add FakeAndroidManifestAsset and UpdateManifest to hide manifest
construction from browser AI tests. Cover early config arrival, built-in
fallbacks, load failures, snapshot identity, session replacement, and
adaptation-backed session preservation.

Re-enable applicable Android Summarizer tests using fake manifest assets
instead of asynchronous fake adaptation overrides.

Component monitoring, disk loading, and delivery integration will follow
in a separate CL tracked by crbug.com/575550015.

[views] Reset ignore_window_pos_changes_ on bounds and state changes

When OnWindowPosChanging() adjusts bounds for fullscreen, maximized
state or a work area change, it sets `ignore_window_pos_changes_` and
posts StopIgnoringPosChanges() to ignore spurious follow-up
::SetWindowPos() calls from Windows. Until that task runs, explicit
SetBounds(), SetSize() and CenterWindow() calls are also discarded,
e.g. right after SetFullscreen(false) or Restore().

This CL calls StopIgnoringPosChanges() in SetBounds(), SetSize(),
CenterWindow(), Maximize(), Minimize(), Restore(), SetFullscreen() and
SetAspectRatio(), so that explicit bounds and show state changes
requested by Chrome take effect instead of being discarded.
SetBoundsInternal() is unchanged: its other callers
(OnBackgroundFullscreen(), the background fullscreen restore on
activation, OnDpiChanged()) react to Windows messages rather than
Chrome requests, so they keep their existing behavior.

Exposed by https://crrev.com/c/8590980: in
PresentationReceiverWindowViewBrowserTest.
ModalDialogHostObserversNotified, SetBounds() after
ShowInactiveFullscreen() and ExitFullscreen() was ignored, and the test
only passed thanks to a redundant HandleClientSizeChanged()
notification.

SidePanel: Take the browser window as JniPtr in coordinator

SidePanelCoordinatorAndroidBridge reads the native
BrowserWindowInterface from InitInfo as a raw long and
side_panel_coordinator_android.cc casts it back with reinterpret_cast.
The long is detached from the JniUniquePtr through which
AndroidBrowserWindow owns the native window, so nothing stops a stale
value from reaching C++ as a dangling pointer.

Read InitInfo#nativeBrowserWindow, added in https://crrev.com/c/8620634,
and declare the native parameter as JniPtr<NativeBrowserWindowInterface>
so that JNI Zero hands BrowserWindowInterface* to C++ directly. Behavior
is unchanged, except that passing a destroyed window to native now
throws IllegalStateException in Java instead of using freed memory.

The Java debug log lines, which are behind the side panel logging
flag, no longer print the window address, since Java no longer has it.

TAG=agy
CONV=d7896fff-bb31-4ee0-9555-287077259ab8

SuperSize: Speed up diff.Diff symbol matching and diff_status

1. Add diff._StripNumbers() to fast-path _STRIP_NUMBERS_PATTERN.sub()
   when '$' is not in the symbol name, using str.rstrip('.0123456789')
   rather than running an unanchored regex alternation across 6.4M
   symbol names.
2. Skip padding_pss arithmetic in diff._MatchSymbols() when both
   matched symbols have zero padding.
3. Skip computing DeltaSymbol.pss in DeltaSymbol.diff_status when
   neither symbol has aliases and the before symbol is not padding-only.

Expected speed-up: ~30.0s on create_patched_supersize_diff.py.

930b39a9e7dcb7cc1d9732d168ef24c7a7b4a3de [ diff ] 
SuperSize: Run dwarfdump.CreateAddressSourceMapper in parallel with _AnalyzeElf

native.CreateSymbols previously ran dwarfdump.CreateAddressSourceMapper
synchronously before starting _AnalyzeElf, even though its result is not
used until _AddSourcePathsUsingAddress after _AnalyzeElf completes.

Run dwarfdump.CreateAddressSourceMapper in a background worker via
parallel.ForkAndCall so that dwarfdump execution overlaps with
_AnalyzeElf.

Also only use ninja object paths for source paths when the linker .map
is available (the same condition used to decide whether to run
dwarfdump). Otherwise, a container without a .map in a multi-container
archive would discard its dwarfdump results.

Expected speed-up: ~6.0s wall-clock on ChromePublic.apk (overlaps
dwarfdump execution with _AnalyzeElf).

[html-in-canvas] Fully update when clearing origin-tainted filters

This patch forces an isolation-piercing subtree paint property update
when clearing `ObjectPaintProperties` with an origin-tainted filter
(`Filter()->Filter()->OriginTainted()`), matching `UpdateFilter()` and
similar to https://crrev.com/026bad204a461a059d709ad5b81c20f210c6ea78.

When an element no longer needs paint properties, `InitPaintProperties`
clears `ObjectPaintProperties` before `UpdateFilter()` runs. Without
an isolation-piercing update, descendant effect nodes inside a
`contain: paint` subtree retain stale `IsInTaintedSubtree()` state
after an ancestor's cross-origin filter is removed.

7ed82cc6d7e4b63bf63a316cede7588276e4cce9 [ diff ] 
Printing: Guard deferred PrintWithParams against nested print

When `PrintRenderFrameHelper::PrintWithParams()` defers printing to load
lazy or print-media resources, the `OnPrintWithParamsFinished()`
continuation ran outside `ScopedIPC` and without `print_in_progress_`
set. This allowed page scripts (e.g. via `matchMedia('print')` or
`beforeprint`/`afterprint` listeners) to invoke `window.print()` and
initiate a nested `PrintPreview` or `ScriptedPrint` operation while
`PrintPages()` was on the stack, overwriting `print_pages_params_` or
destroying `PrintRenderFrameHelper`.

To fix this:
- Apply `ScopedIPC` and set `print_in_progress_ = true` for the duration
  of `OnPrintWithParamsFinished()`.
- Store `print_with_params_callback_` and block concurrent print
  entry points while `PrintWithParams()` is pending (and vice versa
  when `print_in_progress_` is set).
- Clone `print_pages_params_->params` instead of holding raw references
  across page rendering calls.

parent
6329072641e7b54c28b3b7d98de6343aa17fd648 [ diff ] 
net: Guard QuicSessionAttemptManager::Job against reentrant completion

In `QuicSessionAttemptManager::OnOriginFrame()`, matching `Job`
instances were collected into a `std::vector<Job*>` before invoking
`OnOriginFrameMatched()` on each entry. Similarly,
`QuicSessionAttemptManager::Job::NotifyRequests()` notifies each waiting
`QuicSessionAttemptRequest` synchronously while `this` remains in
`active_jobs_` and `Job::RemoveRequest()` unconditionally calls
`manager_->OnJobComplete(this)` as soon as `requests_` becomes empty. If
a request's completion callback starts a new request for the same key,
cancels a sibling request on the same `Job`, cancels a request on
another matched `Job`, or destroys the owning `QuicSessionPool`, the
completing `Job` can collide with the new request or be destroyed while
`NotifyRequests()` or `OnOriginFrame()` is still iterating.

To handle reentrant requests, cancellation, and destruction during
notification, move completing `Job` instances from `active_jobs_` to
`completing_jobs_` before notifying waiting requests, defer
`OnJobComplete()` in `RemoveRequest()` while `NotifyRequests()` is
active, guard `Job` with a `WeakPtr` across synchronous completion
callbacks, and hold `base::WeakPtr<Job>` entries in `OnOriginFrame()`.
Also make `~QuicSessionAttemptManager()` keep jobs in `completing_jobs_`
while aborting them so that `RemoveRequest()` can still find requests
cancelled from `ERR_ABORTED` callbacks during teardown.

Parse //DEPS instead of .gclient_entries in private_code_test

Previously, build/private_code_test/BUILD.gn declared
//../.gclient_entries as an input to list_gclient_deps.py. Because
.gclient_entries resides outside the src/ checkout root, building with
DEPOT_TOOLS_USE_VIRTUAL_BUILD_PATH=1 failed when resolving
../../../.gclient_entries from the virtualized build directory, and
list_gclient_deps.py had to be denylisted from Siso remote execution.

Switch list_gclient_deps.py to parse //DEPS (plus checked-out internal
recursedeps passed via --deps-file from BUILD.gn), validate recursedeps
against an audited allowlist, and remove list_gclient_deps.py from the
Siso remote execution denylist. Add bidirectional LINT.IfChange /
LINT.ThenChange annotations between //DEPS and list_gclient_deps.py to
ensure the recursedeps lists remain synchronized. Also fix the
'# ERROR: ' prefix emitted on parse failures so that
private_code_test.py detects deferred parse errors as intended.

Open the help homepage for generic help contexts

Before this CL, enabling UsePLinkInHelp opened every help context via
p-link (Open-to-Content). Generic entry points such as the app menu
(mobile_webpage, mobile_new_tab, ...) then opened a specific article
instead of the help homepage, which hid the "Send feedback" entry
(crbug.com/562480690).

Per Audit #2 in go/clank-user-help-plink, add
R.array.help_contexts_using_homepage for generic contexts that open the
help homepage; all others use p-links. Delegates use the new
HelpAndFeedbackLauncherDelegate.getPLinkHelpUrlIfSupported().

UsePLinkInHelp stays disabled by default.

[actor] Add FilePickerInterceptor

Add a WebContentsUserData that holds the files an actor task has staged
for upload, and answers the target frame's next file chooser request
with them instead of showing the native file picker.
FileSelectHelper::RunFileChooser() consults it first.

The staged files are held in memory by storage::InMemoryFileRegistry and
are handed to the page as filesystem: URLs, so nothing is written to
disk. Requests from other documents, e.g. cross-origin subframes, are
not answered. The staging is dropped if no file chooser request arrives
before a timeout or if the page is navigated away from. Files that were
handed out are kept for as long as the document that received them.

The interceptor is only consulted when kGlicActorFileUploadTool is
enabled. FileUploadTool installs it in a follow-up CL.

Mojo C++: Remove base::debug::Alias() from IPCStableHash() functions

Shrinks Android arm32 size by 70kb.

Each mojom method has an IPCStableHash() function whose address is used
to identify the method after symbolization. Its body stored the hash to
the stack and called base::debug::Alias() to prevent identical code
folding. However, returning a unique hash already makes each function
body unique, so the alias is not needed.

This shrinks each function from 24 bytes to 10 bytes on arm32.

[Omnibox] Add OmniboxVoicePlateIntent feature flag

Add a disabled-by-default feature flag that will gate handing Chrome
voice search to the Android Google App Voice Plate. This covers the
Omnibox, New Tab Page and toolbar mic buttons. With the flag on, the
Google app handles voice capture and transcription, and Chrome
navigates directly to the results.

The flag is exposed to Java via OmniboxFeatures and listed in
chrome://flags (#omnibox-voice-plate-intent). It has no effect yet.
Follow-up changes add the Voice Plate intent and wire it into voice
recognition.

[MFVEA] Free encoder activation resources after capability probing

Capability probing leaked the encoder objects it created: the temporal
layer probe activated every enumerated encoder but never called
ShutdownObject(), and the enumeration dropped a reference per returned
activation. The leaked activations kept the created MFTs, their worker
threads and GPU allocations alive for the lifetime of the GPU process.

Shut down probed activations on scope exit, adopt the MFTEnum2()/MFTEnumEx() references into ComPtrs, and drop the manual Release() in Destroy() that is handled by the ComPtr destructor. (It has to be dropped since previously it fortunately offsets the leak, but now if kept, is a double Release).

Also remove the redundant temporal layer probing helper method.

Webium: migrate ReloadButton to InitialWebUIMetricsDispatcher

Following the design of
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ae7OUsWMAr1WmyNFOjmSeqXfj_0lpiIRDn0xiC-ntJE/edit?usp=sharing&resourcekey=0-SLmwBU1D-cgJWsOZjVHn4w
(googlers only), this CL routes all ReloadButton metrics, for both the
native Views button and the WebUI toolbar, through
`InitialWebUIMetricsDispatcher`, so that the startup vs. new window
decision is made in a single place.

- `InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager` now owns an
  `InitialWebUINativeMetricsDispatcher`, exposed via
  `GetMetricsDispatcher()`. The toolbar's native `ReloadButton` reports
  creation and paints through it (`WebAppNavigationButtonContainer`
  passes `nullptr`, as `InitialWebUIWindowMetricsManager` is only
  created for normal browser windows).
- `WebUIToolbarWebView` reports creation through the toolbar
  WebContents' `InitialWebUIWebContentsMetricsDispatcher`, which already
  handles its commit and paints.
- The manager no longer decides whether a reload button paint is a
  startup paint. `OnReloadButtonFirstPaint()` and
  `OnReloadButtonFirstContentfulPaint()` now take an explicit
  `is_startup` argument from the dispatcher, and
  `OnReloadButtonCreated()` is removed.

No histogram changes are intended.

usb/hid: Reset SW tick clock in browsertests

WebUsbExtensionBrowserTest and WebHidExtensionBrowserTest pass a stack-
allocated SimpleTestTickClock to AdvanceClockAfterRequestTimeout() in
DeviceConnectAndOpenDeviceWhenServiceWorkerStopped, which stores the
pointer in ServiceWorkerVersion::tick_clock_. Because the tests leave an
active device connection open when exiting the test body,
ServiceWorkerVersion outlives the stack clock and dereferences a
dangling pointer during teardown.

Reset the tick clock to the default instance before the stack clock goes
out of scope, and re-enable the WebHID test on Linux and ChromeOS.

SuperSize: Avoid nested property calls in pss / size properties

Symbol.pss, Symbol.pss_without_padding, Symbol.padding_pss,
DeltaSymbol.pss and DeltaSymbol.size are called tens of millions of
times when diffing and describing (e.g. via DeltaSymbol.diff_status and
sorting). Compute them from fields directly rather than through
num_aliases / size_without_padding / repeated before_symbol and
after_symbol lookups.

Expected speed-up: diff.Diff(sort=True) + describe.GenerateLines() on
two ~2.1M-symbol .size files (as done by trybot_commit_size_checker.py):
58.87s -> 53.45s (identical output).

[PA] Move ThreadCacheStats from ThreadCache to PartitionTls

Move ThreadCacheStats out of ThreadCache and into PartitionTls, placed
directly after thread_cache_storage in the same per-thread allocation.
This shrinks sizeof(ThreadCache) by sizeof(ThreadCacheStats) (88 bytes,
or 984 bytes with THREAD_CACHE_ALLOC_STATS) and keeps statistics per
thread rather than per ThreadCache.

When kMaxThreadCacheIndex == 1, ThreadCache::GetEnclosingTls() recovers
the enclosing PartitionTls via pointer arithmetic on `this` using
offsetof(PartitionTls, thread_cache_storage), avoiding an OS TLS lookup
and folding counter updates into a single constant-displacement memory
operand from `this`.

Update kThreadCacheStorageSize in partition_tls.h to match the new
sizeof(ThreadCache) across 64-bit and 32-bit configurations, document
its layout and buildflag terms, and enforce both upper and lower bounds
via two-way static_asserts in ThreadCache::Create().

Accumulate ThreadCacheStats in PartitionTlsRegistry::DumpStats() so each
thread's counters are counted once regardless of ThreadCache count.

c2946ec3a94d797b1b8ec71de7633645426a5652 [ diff ] 
[TabUI] Resolve drag-to-merge cards directly from TabListModel

When dropping a dragged card onto another card in the Grid Tab Switcher,
TabGridItemTouchHelperCallback converted the TabListModel adapter
positions into TabModel representative indices via
getTabCardCountsBefore and looked up the cards via
getRepresentativeTabAt and getRelatedTabList.

That round-trip kept the last unflagged callers of
TabModel#getRepresentativeTabAt and TabListModel#getTabCardCountsBefore
alive, queried TabModel twice per card, and shifted the lookup index
whenever ARCHIVED_TAB_GROUP cards were present in TabListModel (which
getTabCardCountsBefore counted even though they are not in TabModel).
Resolving the dragged and hovered cards directly from TabListModel by
group token or tab ID removes the representative-index conversion and
fetches each card's tabs in a single lookup.

[a11y] Fix ChromeOS Dictation network speech crash

ChromeOS Dictation's NetworkSpeechRecognizer runs in the browser process
without a RenderFrameHost and passes an empty GlobalRenderFrameHostId to
SpeechRecognitionManager. Recent checks in https://crrev.com/c/8407668
and https://crrev.com/c/8586995 abort sessions and fail a child_id CHECK
when no RenderFrameHost is present, causing Dictation to stop on startup
for locales without SODA and leave its start callback pending.

Allow browser-initiated sessions with an empty GlobalRenderFrameHostId
on ChromeOS only when Dictation is active, and run any pending start
callback with an error if SpeechRecognitionPrivateRecognizer stops
before recognizing.

TEST=content_browsertests --gtest_filter=*SpeechRecognition*
TEST=browser_tests --gtest_filter=*SpeechRecognition*

AX-Relnotes: Fix Dictation crash when using network speech recognition.

[Extensions] Fix UAF in WindowsUpdateFunction::UpdateWindowState()

When updating a browser window's state via chrome.windows.update() (such
as entering or exiting fullscreen), platform window operations can spin
a nested message loop. If a queued close request (for example,
chrome.windows.remove()) executes during that nested loop, the native
window is closed and synchronously destroys the Browser, BrowserView
(ui::BaseWindow), and BrowserExtensionWindowController
(WindowController).

While lower-layer methods (BrowserView::ProcessFullscreen(),
views::Widget::SetFullscreen(), and FullscreenController) already guard
this with WeakPtr, WindowsUpdateFunction::UpdateWindowState() and
WindowsUpdateFunction::Run() held raw pointers to browser,
browser_window, and window_controller and continued dereferencing them
after the window was destroyed.

Expose WindowController::GetWeakPtr() and check if
BrowserWindowInterface and WindowController are alive across window
state transitions in WindowsUpdateFunction::UpdateWindowState() and
WindowsUpdateFunction::Run(), returning early with kNoCurrentWindowError
if the window was destroyed.

Also add WeakPtr liveness checks across Show() / ShowInactive() and
state transitions in WindowsCreateFunction::OnBrowserWindowCreated(),
TabsCreateFunction::OnBrowserWindowCreated(), and CreateAndShowBrowser()
in open_tab_helper.cc.

vaapi: Resubmit the quality level on every frame for VP8 encoding

The recent CL:8480216 revealed a pre-existing issue in which the Intel
hardware VP8 encoder may produce a corrupted bitstream. The initial
investigation uncovered two potential issues:

1) The iHD "Repak" feature may be faulty and something in that path
   seems to produce a bitstream missing one byte sometimes.

2) The iHD driver resets the quality level every time a
   VAEncSequenceParameterBufferVP8 is submitted. This has the side
   effect of enabling "Repak."

This CL works around (2), and as a side effect, it hopefully addresses
(1) on all our devices.

ipc: Pack ChannelAssociatedGroupController::Endpoint better

In release builds, this class has a 4-byte refcount, which before
this CL was followed with 4 bytes of padding. Move next_sync_message_id_
into these 4 bytes instead.

Reduces the size of Endpoint from 112 to 104 bytes, which lets it
fit into a PartitionAlloc alloc size class of 104 bytes instead of
the next-higher class of 120 bytes.

With five ad-heavy tabs, there are about 10K Endpoint objects, so
this saves about 160 KB in the browser process.

No behavior change.

Revert "[tracing] Use 32 MB default SMB in browser process"

This reverts commit 863c8b75e37897eb59650eb20490ff049eda3e04.

Reason for revert: Revert of 863c8b75e3789 due to deterministic
timeout in BackgroundTracingManagerBrowserTest.RunStartupTracing on
linux-chromeos-chrome.

Failure Link: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8666862232206273553

Original change's description:
> [tracing] Use 32 MB default SMB in browser process
>
> During startup tracing, the default 4 MB producer SMB fills up on
> `CrBrowserMain` before the `TracingService` utility process connects,
> dropping events. Add `kPerfettoBrowserSharedMemorySizeBytes` (default
> 32 MB) and use it when `enable_consumer` is true in
> `PerfettoTracedProcess::SetupClientLibrary`.
>
> While a clean `about:blank` launch only buffers ~3 MB before
> `TracingService` connects (~4.5s), a heavy Windows startup with session
> and extension restore fills 4 MB in 2.1s (~2 MB/s) while
> `TracingService` takes ~14-20s to spawn and drain the SMB, requiring the
> full 32 MB (`kMaxShmSize`) to avoid a startup blind spot.
>
> Tested: `StartupTracingTest` browser tests + verified 0 SMB data loss on
> a 15 MB local `chrome --trace-startup=*` trace.
>

[Omnibox] Disable Mojo ordinal scrambling for AIM eligibility extension

When building the AIM Eligibility component extension from a local
non-official Chromium build (or a different Chrome milestone) and
loading it into an official Chrome build via Component Updater, the
renderer crashes with RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE due to mismatched
Mojo method ordinals:

1. `aim_eligibility.mojom` had message ID scrambling enabled by default
   in official builds (`scramble_message_ids = true`), which salts
   ordinals with `chrome/VERSION`. Set `scramble_message_ids = false` on
   `//c/b/ui/webui/omnibox_internals/aim_eligibility:mojo_bindings` so
   ordinals remain deterministic across builds.
2. When `optimize_webui = true`, `aim_eligibility_extension` bundled
   `color_change_listener.mojom-webui.js` and `time.mojom-webui.js` into
   `app.js`. Exclude both from the extension bundle via so they are
   loaded at runtime from `chrome://resources/`.

Require a left mouse press on the web contents for renderer mouse drags

WebContentsViewAura::StartDragging validated a renderer-initiated mouse
drag with aura::Env::IsLeftMouseButtonDown(), a process-global flag that
reports whether the left button is held anywhere. Several features
armed ad hoc suppressions (e.g.
DesktopDragDropClientOzone::ScopedSuppressForWindowMove) to keep a
compromised renderer from latching a data drag onto a held button that
was not pressed on its web contents, but each suppression had to be
kept exactly in sync with the gesture it protected. For example, on
Linux/X11, WindowEventFilterLinux released its caption click-hold
suppression on any non-drag located event, including a kMouseExited
that a compromised renderer in a Window Controls Overlay app could
manufacture with a popup widget and window.moveTo(). The renderer could
then turn the user's window-move gesture into a drag of attacker data.

EnvInputStateController now also tracks the window the current left
button press was dispatched to, and whether that press has already been
used to start a drag. Non-client presses (which may become window moves)
are not associated with their target. A new
Env::ConsumeLeftMousePressForDrag(window) returns true, and marks the
press as used, only if the left button is down and its press was
dispatched to `window` and is unused. StartDragging uses it for mouse
drags, so the press must have been dispatched to the web contents
itself, and each press can start at most one drag. A press on the window
caption or an app's draggable region, on a menu holding capture, or on
another WebContents no longer satisfies the check, regardless of the
state of any suppression. This mirrors the existing requirement for
touch drags.

Disable SwiftShader by default in headless.

When SwiftShader was disabled in Chrome by default, the intent was to
do the same for all flavors of Chrome, including headless. A couple of
code paths were missed.

Verified with both --headless and --headless=new that SwiftShader is
now disabled by default, and requires --enable-unsafe-swiftshader to
enable it.

Added headless tests ensuring that WebGL and WebGPU are now disabled
by default, and enabled by --enable-unsafe-swiftshader (and, for
WebGPU, --enable-unsafe-webgpu).

[Ad Detection] Record use counter for sticky pop-out video ad detection

Sticky pop-out video ads are among the least preferred formats under
the Better Ads Standards. Dedicated telemetry is needed to understand
prevalence and support potential enforcement.

This CL adds `kStickyPopOutVideoAdDetected`, recorded when a video ad
that was displayed inline visibly moves to stick within the viewport,
e.g., docking in a corner once the user scrolls past it.

`DisplayAdElementMonitor` now tracks the ad's placement (`kUnknown`,
`kInline`, `kSticky`), which may alternate between `kInline` and
`kSticky` once determined:
- `kInline` (new): The ad keeps its document position while the page
  scrolls (beyond the sticky ad detection's lag tolerance), as seen
  within the viewport. Its latest rect relative to the viewport is
  tracked while inline.
- `kSticky`: Set by the existing sticky ad detection, which pauses
  while the ad is sticky and resumes afresh once it's found inline.

A `kInline` -> `kSticky` transition is a pop-out, unless the sticky
ad's rect overlaps the ad's last inline rect by more than half (of the
larger of the two), i.e., it sticks in place.

Drive-by simplification:
Sticky ad detection thresholds are now derived from the ad's current
height rather than the height stored with its anchor. This is a
behaviorally neutral change that simplifies the state tracking.

[views-ax] Add reversible WidgetAXManager disablement

Add support for disabling WidgetAXManager and rebuilding its tree when
it is enabled again. Keep the hosting information, but clear the active
tree, pending updates, and focus observation.

Disable() is synchronous, a native client can request enablement during
teardown, so finish cleanup and then re-enable before Disable() returns.
Disabling while Enable() is running is still not allowed.

Keep WebView observing its manager so it can clear its native accessible
parent before the old tree is released and restore it on re-enable.

This is needed for ignored-root eligibility, but doesn't yet disable
trees based on their RootView's ignored state.

[ReadAloud] Drop the unused audio timestamp from word boundaries

OnWordBoundaryReached no longer carries an audio timestamp over mojo
(dropped in crrev.com/c/8546430), as playback progress is reported
separately via OnPlaybackProgressChanged.

This CL cleans up the utility process:
- Drops `audio_timestamp` from ReadAloudAudioRenderer's
  WordBoundaryCallback and its PumpWordBoundaries() dispatch loop.
- Updates ReadAloudPlaybackController::OnWordBoundaryReached to receive
  only (start_character_offset, end_character_offset).
- Updates ReadAloudAudioRenderer unit tests to drop `audio_timestamp`
  from the Boundary test struct and test expectations while preserving
  all dispatch timing assertions.

[TabStrip] Gather multi-selected tabs outward from primary tab (2/3)

Gather multi-selected tabs outward from the primary tab.
-Previously, MultiTabReorderStrategy#gatherBlock iterated forward
 through selectedTabs from primaryTabModelIndex -
 primaryTabIndexInSelection. When multiple selected tabs appeared
 before the primary tab, earlier moves shifted intermediate unselected
 tabs and prevented later tabs from crossing them, and the primary tab
 itself received a redundant TabModel#moveTab call.
-Now, MultiTabReorderStrategy#gatherBlock iterates right-to-left for
 tabs before the primary tab and left-to-right for tabs after it.
-Unify the mixed-pin partition gathering after the group-merge check.
